topic.angle: The water lily riddle: doubling looks harmless until the last day

panels.text: A riddle French children are given: a water lily grows in a pond, and the plant doubles in size every day.
Left alone, it would smother the pond in 30 days, killing the other living things in the water.
Day after day the plant looks small, so people decide not to worry until it covers half the pond.
Which day is that? The 29th, which leaves only one day to save the pond. Doubling feels slow, then suddenly it is not.

probes.question: A lily doubles every day and covers half the pond on day 29. When is the pond fully covered?
True or false: with daily doubling, the lily covers a quarter of the pond the day before it covers half.

claims.claim: French children are given a water lily riddle: the plant doubles every day and would smother the pond in 30 days
claims.quote: The plant doubles in size every day and, if left alone, it would smother the pond in 30 days killing all the other living things in the water.

claims.claim: Because the growth looks small, nobody worries until it covers half the pond; that is day 29, one day left
claims.quote: The 29th day, leaving only one day to save the pond.

claims.claim: Doubling feels slow, then suddenly it is not
claims.quote: the apparent suddenness with which an exponentially growing quantity approaches a fixed limit

claims.claim: Probe: half covered on day 29 means full on day 30; the day before half it is a quarter
claims.note: Verified by calculation: doubling daily: day 30 = 2 x day 29 = full; day 28 = half of day 29 = a quarter.
